issues.title: [Bug]: readonly initializer reentry can mutate a constructed object
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: prints 2. Clean-context spec check: self.init from a method is legal (§6.8.1.5), but readonly-class objects are read-only (§8.6) and the read-only bit is fixed once constructed (§5.1), so the store through self.init must not succeed. The spec doesn't say whether that's a compile error or a runtime panic. Classed as backend because the runtime store into a read-only object does not panic. Proposed parent: #1043 (readonly class values are not treated as readonly at runtime). Related: #1196.

issues.title: [Bug]: nil value for an optional field is rejected in a mapping constructor
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible type: expected int, got nil|int
  --> main.bal:10:16
ballerina: compilation contains errors
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: SEMANTIC_ERROR 'expected int, got nil|int'. §6.7.2 lets the value of an optional non-nil field be nil, in which case the field is not added; expected {"b":2}. The type checker rejects a valid program. No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: module variable operand is read after a later call in the same expression changes it
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: {"a":100,...}, [100,9], 109. Clean-context spec check: the list case is clearly required (§6.7.1 evaluates members in order), so [100,9] is wrong. For the mapping constructor and '+', the spec doesn't state the order explicitly, though the natural left-to-right reading supports the issue. Root cause is BIR generation: module-variable loads are emitted as operand refs and read after later calls in the same expression, so the generated BIR is wrong (frontend). Related: #1217 (compound assignment lvexpr order), not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: unary - and ~ on a nil-lifted singleton keep the singleton type
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: compiles and prints -1. A nil-lifted unary '-' on a 1|() operand has type int? with no singleton typing (§6.2.5/§6.22.1), so assigning it to -1|() must be a compile error. Type checker bug. #1090 (closed) is different.

issues.title: [Bug]: string template with non-string interpolations is not singleton-typed
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible type: expected "a1", got string
 --> main.bal:5:15
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible type: expected string:Char, got string
 --> main.bal:6:21
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: two SEMANTIC_ERRORs. §6.6.1 plus §6.2.4 singleton typing make string `a${1}` have type "a1" and `${7}` have type "7" (a string:Char), so the program is valid. Type checker bug. Related singleton-typing issues: #1262, #1457, #1046.

issues.title: [Bug]: `readonly & T` has no filler value (list filling panics with "no filler value")
issues.output:
error: no filler value
        at main(main.bal:5)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: runtime panic 'no filler value' at a[1] = [7]. The filler for readonly & T is the read-only filler of T (§5.8.1/§5.9.1 FillMember), so it should print [[],[7]] then true. The reproducer fails in the runtime (values/list.go), so classed as backend. The issue also notes the compile-time tuple variant ('[int, readonly & int[]] t = [1]' rejected in semantics/internal/common), which needs a matching frontend fix.

issues.title: [Bug]: cloneWithType/fromJsonWithType with a union of structural types picks a member that needs lossy conversion over an exact match
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: {"a":2}, [2], {"a":2} (1.5 silently rounded into the int member). Clean-context spec check against lang.value cloneWithType/fromJsonWithType: the core claim holds and lossy rounding is wrong. But under the doc's rule (the member must be determinable as for list/mapping constructors), both members fit, so the strict result is an error, not the {"a":1.5} annotated in the reproducer. The fix should settle this (the issue itself acknowledges the strict reading). Related: #657 (declaration-order ambiguity).

issues.title: [Bug]: 'self' is accepted in a class field initializer
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: compiles and prints 1. self is bound only within a method-defn-body (§6.8.1.2); a field initializer is not one, so this must be a compile error ('undefined symbol self'). Front end accepts an invalid program.

issues.title: [Bug]: 'service on' an error value crashes with a Go interface conversion
issues.output:
error: interface conversion: values.BalValue is *values.Error, not *values.Object
        at init(main.bal:25)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: runtime crash 'interface conversion: values.BalValue is *values.Error, not *values.Object' at init. §8.3.2: if a service-decl 'on' expression evaluates to an error, module initialization fails with that error. Compilation succeeds and the crash is during interpretation, so not frontend-crash. Listener registration and attach are generated in desugar (desugar/desugar.go buildServiceInitStmts) without an error check, so the generated code is wrong (frontend). Could be argued backend.

issues.title: [Bug]: a listener registered more than once is started once per registration
issues.output:
attach ll
attach ll
main
start ll
start ll
start ll
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: 'start ll' printed 3 times. §8.3.2: registering the same object multiple times is the same as registering it once. Registration into $moduleListeners is emitted by desugar (buildListenerRegistration) with no identity dedupe, so frontend. Same area as #1559/#1561 (all from the #1516 review), not duplicates.

issues.title: [Bug]: listener in a non-listener variable used in 'service on' is never started
issues.output:
attach final-var
main
(`start final-var` never printed; process keeps running)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: 'attach final-var', 'main', then 'start final-var' is never printed. Every service-decl 'on' value is registered as a module listener (§8.3.2) and started in the listening phase (§8.3). Desugar only registers module 'listener' declarations, and service 'on' values that aren't such declarations never reach $moduleListeners, so frontend. Same area as #1560/#1561.
